gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much AC energy these TT-30 stations actually delivered in named tests: OutdoorGearLab measured 3,790 Wh from the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (about 92.5% of 4,096 Wh), StorageReview and Notebookcheck got 2,980 Wh and 2,905 Wh from Anker's 3,840 Wh F3800 (about 76-78%), and Outdoor Life got 2,290 Wh from the BLUETTI Apex 300 (83% of 2,765 Wh), so the DELTA Pro 3 delivers roughly 800 Wh more than the Anker despite only 256 Wh more rated capacity.
standout_why: Compared against rvpartsgiant.com (power-station-30-amp-rv-plug), outagereadyhq.com (best-portable-power-station-for-rv) and wattmatch.io (portable-power-station-for-30-amp-rv), the three RV-specific results ChatGPT got. All three use maker spec sheets only; none cites a single independent measurement of delivered Wh, efficiency or idle draw. outagereadyhq and ChatGPT's own answer apply a flat 85% usable-energy assumption to every unit, and wattmatch divides rated Wh by watts. The EcoFlow pages are maker claims; the Solar Waypoint and StationArena comparisons are spec tables.
decides: Confirms the DELTA Pro 3 as the pick and widens its lead: on measured output it runs a 1,200 W rooftop AC about 3.2 h (3,790 Wh / 1,200 W) against about 2.4-2.5 h for the F3800 family (2,905-2,980 Wh), 2.2 h for the DELTA 3 Ultra Plus (2,610 Wh) and 1.9 h for the Apex 300 (2,290 Wh). The flat 85% rule in ChatGPT's table understates the DELTA Pro 3 (2.9 h) and overstates the Anker, whose rated 3,840 Wh looks close to EcoFlow's but measures about 800 Wh lower. Idle draw (Solar Lab: 22 W on the DELTA 3 Ultra, 58 W on the Jackery 5000 Plus, 80 W on the original F3800) also matters for overnight boondocking.

findings.label: Measured AC energy delivered (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.value: 3,790 Wh of 4,096 Wh rated (about 92.5%; OGL lists 93% usable)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 Review (OutdoorGearLab, Kenji Mowrey, 2026-01-13)
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab measured AC output from full to cutoff; 3,790 / 4,096 = 92.5% (the text says 'over 93%'). Same review: full AC charge about 3-3.2 h, measured charge rate 1,293 Wh/h, peak input over 1,600 W. 1,200 W AC load: 3,790 / 1,200 = 3.2 h.

findings.label: Measured discharge capacity (Digital Trends)
findings.value: 3.7 kWh average over multiple cycles; about 5 kWh drawn from the wall for a 0-100% charge
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 review (Digital Trends, Simon Sage, 2024-06-25)
findings.note: Reviewer's own cycles; full charge took about 3 h. Round trip implied 3.7 / 5 = about 74% (our arithmetic, not the reviewer's). A second independent reading close to OutdoorGearLab's 3,790 Wh.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX F3800 (original; same 3,840 Wh rating as the F3800 Plus)
findings.label: Measured usable capacity (StorageReview)
findings.value: 2,980 Wh delivered of 3,840 Wh rated (about 78%); 4,930 Wh to charge 0-100%
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800: Do We Really Need Gas Generators? (StorageReview, Kevin OBrien, 2024-06-21)
findings.note: Delivered energy until inverter cut-off after a 100% charge; 2,980 / 3,840 = 77.6%; round trip 2,980 / 4,930 = 60%. Measured on the original F3800, not the F3800 Plus; no F3800 Plus discharge measurement was found. 1,200 W AC load: 2,980 / 1,200 = 2.5 h. UPS transfer measured 13 ms / 14 ms.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX F3800 (original; same 3,840 Wh rating as the F3800 Plus)
findings.label: Measured usable capacity, charge energy and noise (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 2,905 Wh delivered of 3,840 Wh (about 75%); 4,669 Wh to charge 1-100%; about 42 dB at 1 m at 3,000 W
findings.source_title: Anker Solix F3800 hands-on review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2024-08-27, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Discharge at a constant ~260 W until shutdown at 1% (about 11 h); Notebookcheck notes smaller stations usually reach 85-90%. Full charge about 1 h 45 min at up to 2,966 W input; Notebookcheck says about 62% of the AC energy consumed was reusable. Original F3800, not the Plus.

findings.label: Measured output in high-draw test (Outdoor Life)
findings.value: 2,290 Wh of 2,765 Wh claimed (83%); AC recharge about 2 h
findings.source_title: Bluetti Apex 300: The Latest Entry in the Stackable Power Station Wars (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster, 2025-05-20)
findings.note: Dehumidifier load metered with a Kill-a-Watt until the station quit. Same test in the table: Anker SOLIX C1000 90%, Jackery Explorer 1000 Plus 86%, Goal Zero Yeti 700 83%. 1,200 W AC load: 2,290 / 1,200 = 1.9 h. TT-30R not tested.

findings.product: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra Plus (Ultra with the same 3,072 Wh rating)
findings.label: Measured discharge and recharge (StorageReview)
findings.value: 2,610 Wh delivered of 3,072 Wh (about 85%); 3,540 Wh to recharge fully; UPS transfer 8.25 ms
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus & Ultra Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-09-30)
findings.note: Measured on the Ultra Plus; StorageReview reports about 85% discharge and about 87% recharge efficiency. 1,200 W AC load: 2,610 / 1,200 = 2.2 h.

findings.label: Measured idle draw, efficiency and charge time (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 22 W idle (about 5.7 days idling); about 82% efficiency; 0-100% in 2 h on a household plug
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra Review: A Solid Performer at a Reasonable Price (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab's own tests; no reviewer name or date on the page. Same page: the BLUETTI Elite 300 took about 2 h 45 min to charge. The 30 A outlet was not load-tested.

findings.label: Measured idle draw and AC-start test (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 58 W idle with the inverter on (about 3.5 days idling); struggled to start a 10,000 W-surge air conditioner; ran 8,000-9,500 W loads for 20-30 s
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Real Competition for the Anker F3800 and DELTA Pro Ultra? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: No reviewer name or date on the page. The same review compares it with 'the F3800's 80W idle rate' (original F3800). Solar Lab lists a 50 A plug limited to 30 A and an L14-30 port, no TT-30R, so a TT-30 RV cord needs an adapter.

findings.label: Measured house-load test and UPS switchover (Android Authority)
findings.value: about 3,750 W pulled with all of the reviewer's gear on; UPS switch about 20 ms; under 700 W for a fridge, PC and lights
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus review (Android Authority, Jonathan Feist, 2025-05-15)
findings.note: Home-backup use, not RV; no usable-Wh discharge test. The TT-30R outlet was not tested (rvpartsgiant states Anker rates it 120 V 25 A, up to 3,000 W).

unsourced: An independent discharge (usable Wh) or idle-draw measurement of the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus itself: The Solar Lab's F3800 Plus review defers testing; a PCMag figure (about 4,248 Wh with one expansion battery, 30-40 W self-draw) is quoted secondhand only, and pcmag.com could not be opened.

Any named reviewer's load test through the TT-30R outlet itself (e.g. 3,000-3,600 W sustained, or an RV rooftop AC start on shore cord) for the DELTA Pro 3, Apex 300 or F3800 Plus: Digital Trends, RV.com, CleanTechnica, Outdoor Life and Android Authority describe the port but did not load it.

A measured usable-Wh figure for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus and a measured idle draw for the DELTA Pro 3 and Apex 300 (Notebookcheck's Apex 300 review is a 230 V EU unit and reports only charge wattage: 2,330 W Turbo, 1,442 W Auto, 508 W Silent).
